extra_sources.locator: Figure 17 insights, printed p.26 (PDF p.28); source DWR (2025) GSL Water Budget

extra_sources.title: GSL Basin Integrated Plan Work Plan Appendix J
extra_sources.quote: Estimates of evaporation from GSL have ranged from 2,000,000 to 5,000,000 acre-feet per year.

arithmetic: 45 in/12 = 3.75 ft (model 3.77). M&T 2012: 1.14 m x 3.281 = 3.74 ft (saline evaporation depth, 1950-2010 mean). DWR/Strike 2026: 2,733 KAF over a 1989-2024 mean area of roughly 1,450-1,500 sq mi (~930-960k acres by the model's own area anchors at ~4,197 ft) gives ~2.85-2.95 ft, i.e. lower.
notes: Two independent long-period estimates (USGS 1978; Mohammed & Tarboton 2012) both give ~45 in/yr saline evaporation, so the central value is confirmed. Caveat: the DWR 2025 water budget quoted by the Strike Team (2,733 KAF/yr, 1989-2024) implies a lower depth (~35 in) if divided by the model's area curve; and DWR says GSL evaporation is very uncertain (2-5 MAF/yr). Within the model only (evap_gross - precip_lake)/inflow_efficiency is fixed by the USU calibration, so sweeping evap_gross alone (3.4-4.1) breaks calibration and exaggerates its 7.6 ft swing; consider sweeping it jointly with precip/efficiency or re-deriving baseline after each draw. If swept alone, a low of ~2.9-3.0 would reflect the DWR budget.

locator: Press release on NBER Working Paper w35270 (Harris, Edwards, Hernandez-Cortes), Sept 10 2026

publisher: National Bureau of Economic Research via Utah Business

extra_sources.title: Potential Costs of Declining Water Levels at Great Salt Lake Could be in the Billions (summary of ECONorthwest 2019 for GSL Advisory Council)
extra_sources.quote: further declines, particularly those over a long period, could result in losses totaling $1.69 billion to $2.17 billion per year

extra_sources.title: Most Utahns are willing to open their wallets for the Great Salt Lake
extra_sources.quote: Utahns are collectively willing to pay up to $162 million per year across the state's 1.1 million households

extra_sources.title: Great Salt Lake Data and Insights Summary
extra_sources.quote: Additional 800 KAF/year inflow ... the additional inflow needed to fill Great Salt Lake to the minimum healthy lake level (4,198 feet) by 2055

arithmetic: ECONorthwest midpoint ($1.69+2.17)/2 = $1.93B/yr / 790-800 KAF = ~$2,410-2,440/AF (range $2,110-2,750/AF using 790 KAF). NBER health-only: $600-1,800/AF. Weber WTP: $162M/800 KAF = ~$200/AF (non-use only).
notes: No source the model cites (DWS jobs, BEA GDP, GSL industry page, Wilkes dust study, Weber WTP) states $2,440/AF or gives the arithmetic. The figure can be reproduced as ECONorthwest's (2019) $1.69-2.17B/yr cost of decline divided by the ~800 KAF/yr added inflow the Strike Team says is needed. But that numerator is mostly gross output (mineral extraction $1.3B), not net welfare, and it is in 2019 dollars. The 2026 NBER estimate ($600-1,800/AF for health alone) is the only published per-AF value found, and it supports a value of the right order. Suggest citing ECONorthwest + NBER explicitly, labelling 2,440 as derived from them, and widening low to ~600. The ECONorthwest PDF (fogsl.org) returned HTML, so the figures are quoted from Audubon's summary of it. The NBER PDF was bot-blocked, so the figures come from the press release.

arithmetic: Dedicated/delivered increments: 2021-25 average (163,468-18,386)/4 = 36.3 KAF/yr; 2024-25 = +14.2 KAF; Trust transactions 2023-25 = +4.2 KAF/yr. Bracket ~5-35 KAF/yr; 25 sits within it.
notes: Growth in dedicated deliveries is lumpy. The 2023-24 jump came mostly from in-lake mineral-extraction water rights converted to sovereign-land uses (Compass, FFSL, Morton; see the DMP Table 2), not from river shepherding. Growth in actual river-shepherded leases (the Trust) is only ~4 KAF/yr. 25 KAF/yr is plausible as a policy-driven upper-middle value. Range 0-80 is wide but defensible.

quote: Average precipitation inches ... 15.52 (394) [annual, Salt Lake City Intl Airport, 1991-2020 normals]
source_title: Climate of Salt Lake City (NOAA NCEI 1991-2020 normals table)

extra_sources.title: Water budget and water-surface fluctuations, Great Salt Lake, Utah (OFR 78-912)
extra_sources.quote: about 900,000 acre-feet from direct precipitation

arithmetic: 15 in/12 = 1.25 ft; NOAA normal 15.52 in = 1.29 ft. Arnow: 2.9 MAF evap at 45 in implies a mean area of 2.9e6/3.75 = 773k acres; 900k AF / 773k ac = 1.16 ft (14 in).
notes: Matches the SLC airport normal and the USGS water-budget-implied ~14 in on the lake. The west side of the lake is drier (a UGS budget table reportedly uses 10 in, but the page was bot-protected and not opened), so lake-wide precipitation may be a little below the airport value. Range 1.0-1.5 is acceptable; a low of ~0.85 would cover the 10-in estimate. Precipitation is sensitive for the same calibration reason as evap_gross.

extra_sources.quote: a 25% decrease in streamflow would reduce lake level by about 66 cm

arithmetic: Illustration: about 2 deg F of additional warming by 2055 x 1.8-6.5%/deg F = 3.6-13% of headwater supply. On roughly 1,665 KAF of lake inflow that is 60-215 KAF/yr; on gross supply it would be larger.

They are qualitative only: precipitation is projected to rise slightly and evaporation and warming to offset it. The 100 KAF/yr value is plausible against the per-degree sensitivity literature, and the 0-300 range brackets it, but it is not sourced. Re-label it as an assumption or derived value, with the UCAR/Bardsley sensitivity as basis.

source_title: An examination of the sensitivity of the Great Salt Lake to changes in inputs

extra_sources.title: Great Salt Lake Data and Insights Summary
extra_sources.quote: No additional inflows ... 4,191.1 feet ... An additional 250 KAF/year results in ... 4,193.7 feet ... An additional 800 KAF/year results in ... 4,198.0

arithmetic: Groundwater only: 1 + 75/1665 = 1.045. Calibration: (E-P)/eff must be about 1665/685.8k ac = 2.43 ft for 4,191.1 ft. Model 2.52/1.03 = 2.447, giving equilibria of 4,191.0 / 4,193.2 / 4,198.2 ft vs published 4,191.1 / 4,193.7-4,193.8 / 4,198.0.
notes: The calibration reproduces the published long-term means to within 0.6 ft, and 1.03 sits in the physically plausible band (groundwater alone gives ~1.045; ungauged tributaries add more). The parameter is collinear with evap_gross and precip_lake.

source_title: Opportunities and Costs for Agricultural Water Optimization in the Great Salt Lake Basin
arithmetic: Per-acre depletion cut as a share of full fallow: cease after June 0.770/1.504 = 0.51; cease after July 0.525/1.504 = 0.35; alfalfa to winter wheat 0.614/1.504 = 0.41; wheel line to SDI 0.394/1.504 = 0.26.
notes: The deepest non-fallow per-acre options in the state report cut about 35-51% of full-season depletion, so 0.5 sits at the top of what is achievable without fallowing. The range 0.25-0.75 is OK, but 0.75 implies near-fallow.
